title: Lists that protect your wallet at the shops
description: A written list is the simplest spending tool there is, because it makes the decisions at home where they are cheapest.

body.heading: Decide at the kitchen table
paragraphs: Every item on a list was chosen in calm conditions, with the cupboards in view and the budget in mind. Every item grabbed in the aisle was chosen in a hurry, surrounded by packaging designed to be chosen. The list simply moves the decision to the better room.
This applies well beyond food: a list for clothes, gifts or household items, written before the shopping trip or the browsing session, works the same quiet magic.

body.heading: Write a list that works
paragraphs: Keep a running list where the household can add to it all week: a pad on the fridge or a shared phone note. Things get bought once, in the right quantity, instead of twice from memory and once from hope.
Organise the list roughly by shop layout if you know it. A list you can follow in order means fewer laps past the tempting shelves, and a shorter trip overall.

body.heading: The rule that makes it real
paragraphs: A list only protects you if unlisted items face a question. Not a ban, a question: do we need this today, and what does it replace? Some unlisted things pass the test happily, and that is fine; the pause is the protection.
For bigger unplanned temptations, the list has a companion rule: it goes on next week's list, and if it still looks essential after a few days at home, it gets bought with a clear conscience.

takeaway: Write it at home, keep it where everyone can add, and make unlisted items answer one friendly question.
